assumptions.basis: DATE 2026-11-04 revision (red-team C2/C3). FY2026E 47.0 Mt reconciles the 9M-2026 delivery with the inventory build and the fourth quarter instead of defaulting to the prior-year Q4 pace. 9M sales were 32.23 Mt (F36, S11) against 9M production of 34.41 Mt (F37, S11), a 2.18 Mt production-over-sales build, and third-quarter production alone ran 14.96 Mt after 19.45 Mt in H1 (F73, S17). Taking Q4 sales at the Q3 production run-rate, 32.23 + 14.96 = 47.19 Mt, gives FY2026E 47.0 Mt: the inventory is carried, not assumed sold, and the 49.51 Mt plan (F42, S11) would need a further ~2.1 Mt draw plus a Q4 rail step-up (the 2026 transport target is 41.0 Mt against 27.08 Mt in 9M, F47, S11), neither of which has been delivered. From FY2027E the base holds 49.5 Mt, the company's 2026 production/sales target (49.55/49.51 Mt, F42, S11) carried forward as the last sourced forward level: the 2027 RKAB plan is filed with ESDM but not approved and no 2027 tonnage is published (S19, S20), so this is the 2026 target held forward, not an approved 2027 plan. The report quantifies the approval risk at a 46 Mt delivered run-rate and at the permanent Banko Barat permit loss. FY2028E onward holds 49.5 Mt for the same reason. The 9M shortfall is a 2026 execution miss, not evidence of a permanently lower capability: production fell 4.1% to 34.41 Mt (F37) while the plan was reaffirmed (F42), and Q3 production recovered 17% q/q (F73). No volume upside is added in the bull: 49.5 Mt is already the approved 2026 target (S3, S11) and no approved headroom above it is disclosed, so the bull carries price and payout, not tonnage.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: DATE 2026-11-04 revision (red-team C8). FY2026E 0.4635 is the COAL-ONLY ratio, correcting the earlier 0.471 which was total 9M revenue over tonnes and therefore carried the non-coal book in the numerator while the model adds other_revenue separately — a double count of about 1.5% of coal revenue. Derivation: the disclosed 9M revenue of Rp35.20trn (F35, S11) includes the non-coal book (H1 other-activity revenue Rp357.6bn, F19 less F26; about Rp550bn for nine months), leaving coal revenue of about Rp34.65trn on 32.23 Mt of sales (F36), about Rp1,075,000/t. Denominator: the coal deck's 2026 Newcastle average of about US$131.9/t (Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4, Q3 138.1), translated at the deck's FY2026E rupiah of 17,570: 1,075,000 / (131.9 x 17,570) = 0.4639, carried at 0.4635, the coal-only ratio the desk previously had. The release's ASP +18% against Newcastle +25% and ICI-3 +26% (F51, S11) confirms that the medium-CV, 51.5%-domestic book (F50, F15) captured less than the high-CV benchmark. FY2026E applies the ratio to the full-year benchmark of US$137.0. That benchmark is the coal deck's dated entry (reviewed 2026-10-26) and is 3.8% above the nine-month average because it embeds the deck's Q4-2026 forward curve (Oct 149.35-150.35, Nov 151.55-151.75, Dec 152.75-153.30); at a stable ratio it reproduces the full-year ASP, and no Q4 lag is added. Because the model is annual, filling the nine months from the print loads that price uplift into the residual fourth quarter, which is why the implied Q4 profit runs above the third quarter's run-rate. Section 3 discloses that implied Q4 net profit, margin and ASP and gives the sensitivity with Q4 held at the nine-month price: FY2026E net profit Rp6,295.9bn, DPS Rp328.1 and a dividend-capacity anchor of Rp2,781, about a fifth below the base. The Q4 price is the deck's forward, not a contracted price and not a wider margin, and that is the signpost to monitor. FY2027E 0.497 interpolates between the 9M observation and the FY2025A calibration 0.5175 at the deck's lower FY2027E benchmark of US$118.0; from FY2028E the model holds the FY2025A calibration (realised Rp922,499/t on 45.43 Mt over the FY2025A Newcastle average of US$108.4/t), the last full actual year, to lt, as the desk rule requires: the last full actual year sets the long-run ratio, and the 2026 compression is the war-premium year unwinding. The drift FY2026E -> FY2030E is +11.7%, above the engine's 10% ratio threshold, so it is justified in qc_justifications.drift.realisation: the 2026 compression is the measured 9M ratio (F35/F36, S11) and the long-run level is the last full actual year's calibration (F13/F1, S5), not an unsourced glide. DATE 2026-10-30 update: the single-export-channel rule does not move this ratio. From 1 January 2027 coal exports must run through the state exporter PT DSI under PP 24/2026 and Permendag 15/2026 (S12, S14), but DSI states it does not take a margin and will charge only a service fee whose size is not published (S16), PTBA says it is aligning its electronic reporting with the customs system and the DSI platform (S13), and existing export contracts continue (S15). No fee or haircut is loaded because none is quantified; the fee and the go-live risk sit in the report's risk and monitoring sections (S12, S16).

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: DATE 2026-11-04 revision (red-team C4). 0.35 is derived from the disclosed PLN revenue and volume data, replacing the earlier 0.27 heuristic (half the domestic upper bound), which sat below the company's own evidence. The deck's US$70/t ceiling is a nominal power-station price (d.coal.dmo_cap, lt 70, no escalation) and is charged to the PLN/power-station part of the book. PLN-group revenue was Rp10,803bn, 30.7% of 9M consolidated revenue (F67/F76, S21), and 33.8% of FY2025 coal revenue (Rp14,429.2bn of Rp41,909.1bn, F58/F13, S5). Because PLN pays a below-average price, its VOLUME share must exceed its revenue share: at the average coal price the implied shares are 30.7% (9M) and 34.4% (FY2025), and 34-43% at a 10-20% discount. The base takes 0.35, the low end of that disclosed range, rather than the 0.27 that lay below every reading; domestic sales were 51.5% of 9M volume (F50, S11), so the cap is still not charged to the whole domestic book. The share is held at 0.35 in every scenario: the tails move d.coal.dmo_cap a fifth either way, so the scenario mirror is on the cap level, not the share. The value effect is small but real: the engine's run at 0.35 lowers the life DCF by about 1% against 0.27, at 0.45 by about 1.4%, and at 0.54 it truncates the DCF at FY2051E; all three are shown in report section 4. The realised ratio (calibrated on actuals) already embeds today's domestic power pricing, so the cap is a second-order term, not an inert one.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: DATE 2026-10-29 revision. 5.63x is the company's own 2026 target and the 9M-2026 run-rate: the strip ratio fell from 5.98x to 5.59x in the nine months, against a 5.63x full-year target (F41/F42, S11), not the FY2025A actual of 6.06x (F16). It is the intensity factor that multiplies cost_per_bcm; the cost split is re-derived below so the FY2026E total still ties to the 9M run-rate, with the lower strip intensity offset inside other_cost_unit and the fuel link (fuel prices +36% yoy, F54/S11). No grade or mine-plan drift is asserted.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: IDR 50,000/bcm (about US$3.0/bcm at the FY2025A rate), the sector norm for Indonesian open-pit overburden removal by contractors — the same US$3.0/bcm the COAL peer set uses. PTBA does not disclose a per-bcm rate, so the split between this and other_cost_unit is a proxy chosen so that strip_ratio x cost_per_bcm plus other_cost_unit lands the FY2025A LK cash cost. Held flat in nominal terms; the engine grows it at the IDR long-run inflation scalar after FY2030E.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: engine default constant — PTBA does not break out fuel; sector norm retained

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: IDR 374,738/t: the balancing item that brings total cash cost to the LK-calibrated level, re-derived for the 5.63x strip ratio. Derivation unchanged: FY2025A cost of revenues Rp36,394,624m (S5 p.128) less royalties to government Rp4,322,659m (F11) less the D&A charged inside cost of revenues (depreciation Rp1,575,007m + amortisation Rp135,726m = Rp1,710,733m, S5 p.128) = Rp30,361,232m of group cash operating cost; the cost of the Rp742,638m of other-activity revenue (F13, S5 Catatan 26) is charged separately on the other_cogs line at Rp668,374m (742,638 x (1 - other_margin)), so the coal cash cost is 30,361,232 - 668,374 = Rp29,692,858m; divided by 45.43 Mt (F1) = Rp653,597/t. The strip component at 5.63x and IDR50,000/bcm is Rp281,500/t, and the fuel uplift at the FY2026E brent of 96.0 (30% fuel share, about +41% against FY2025A) is roughly Rp34,600/t, so other_cost_unit = 690,835 - 281,500 - 34,600 = about Rp374,738/t: the FY2026E total stays at the 9M run-rate while the strip decomposition follows the actual. It carries PTBA's heavy haulage and rail/port cost — the H1-2026 LK shows coal transportation services of Rp3,998,563m as the second-largest cash line inside cost of revenues, behind mining services of Rp5,737,978m (S6 Catatan 27a). Held flat in nominal terms, then grown at IDR inflation. DATE 2026-10-30 update: no PT DSI service fee is loaded into cash cost. PP 24/2026 lets the state export channel set a reasonable margin (S16) but no rate is published, so loading one would be an unsourced cost; the item is monitored, not modelled (S12, S16).

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat-regime fallback; not used under tier mode)
assumptions.basis: The LK's effective royalty rate, charged flat on coal revenue. FY2025A: royalties to government Rp4,322,659m (F11, S5 p.128) on coal revenue Rp41,909,086m (F13, S5 p.127) = 10.31%; FY2024A 9.69% (Rp4,077,822m / Rp42,084,008m). The H1-2026 interim confirms it again: Rp2,209,879m of royalties (S6 Catatan 27a) on Rp21,672,370m of coal revenue (S6 Catatan 26) = 10.20%. The owner directive (MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE) requires the LK's effective rate in the base case, so the model is flat here rather than applying the top IUP band to every tonne: PTBA sells 54% of its volume domestically (S7 p.65) off a 2,800-6,100 GAR slate (F15), so its book mixes the low and mid tranches of the PP 19/2025 schedule and the blended paid rate is the most-likely one. All three scenarios keep this flat effective rate: none switches royalty_mode or the schedule, so the bull is not credited with the banded schedule — at its higher realised price the top band would tax coal revenue above the flat rate, so if the flat rate biases the bull at all it flatters it.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A other revenue of Rp742,638m = total revenue Rp42,651,724m less coal revenue Rp41,909,086m (F13, S5) — trading, transport, palm and services across PTBA's subsidiaries (S7). Held flat in nominal terms and escalated at IDR inflation beyond FY2030E.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: IDR 44,334/t = the LK's own consolidated depreciation AND amortisation of Rp2,014,102m in FY2025 (F7, S5 p.159, segment additional disclosures) divided by 45.43 Mt (F1). This is the RESTATEMENT the desk rule demands: the data pack's D&A of Rp300,136m is only ~15% of the real charge, because the IDX direct cash-flow presentation carries no D&A line and the pack picked up a fragment. The segment note is the anchor because PTBA's mine-property depletion is amortised on a unit-of-production basis inside cost of revenues and is not in the income-statement depreciation line. Held flat in real terms, then escalated at IDR inflation.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: IDR 77,159/t = FY2025A capital expenditure of Rp3,505,367m (F9, S5 p.20 cash-flow statement, "perolehan aset tetap dan tanaman produktif") divided by 45.43 Mt (F1). FY2025 was an investment peak — FY2024 capex was Rp1,231,886m (F10), about IDR 28,700/t on that year's volume — because the Tanjung Enim-Kramasan coal-transport project and the downstream/power build ran through the year (S7). We use the last actual, as the rule requires, and flag that it is the top of the recent range in §3 and the sensitivity table; no drifts are asserted.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: DATE 2026-10-30 revision (red-team C8). FY2026E carries the budget top-up that brings total capital spending to the company's own Rp3.64trn 2026 budget (F43, S11): at the 44.0 Mt delivery, capex_unit of IDR77,159/t gives Rp3,395bn, and the Rp245bn balance is added here so the year is funded at the guidance rather than at a volume-times-rate figure. Zero from FY2027E because capex_unit already carries the FY2025A investment peak (the Tanjung Enim-Kramasan transport build and the downstream/power spend, S7); adding it again would double count. The gain to FCFF is a fraction of the per-share DCF, well inside model tolerance.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt)) — FY2025A was 21.6% (tax Rp813,973m on pbt Rp3,773,209m, S5)

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: engine default constant — no disclosed borrowing plan; PTBA is close to net cash

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items (recurring associate income)
assumptions.basis: DATE 2026-10-29 revision (QC Q3). Carries the recurring share of associates and joint ventures so forecast profit, DPS and the dividend anchor are on a consolidated basis: 9M-2026 associate income was Rp581.31bn, +75% yoy (F48, S11), so the full-year run-rate is about Rp775bn (581.31 x 4/3). The stakes are added at book in the bridge and the DCF does not capitalise this below-the-line income, so there is no double count; it enters pbt and therefore np and the dividend. Held flat in nominal terms, then escalated at IDR inflation. One-off items are not included.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Held at 0.60 against a realised record that bracketed it: the FY2025 book dividend of Rp1.31trn / Rp114.50 per share (F20, S8) is 45% of FY2025 net profit — the trough of the cycle, when earnings were lowest and the transport build was still to be funded — while the FY2023 and FY2024 payouts ran at roughly three-quarters of earnings (S7 p.31, the annual report's dividend history). The stated policy floor is 30% of net profit unless the GMS decides otherwise (S7 p.242). 0.60 is not the cautious pick: it sits above both the policy floor and the most recent (low-year) print and below the boom-year record, and it is the mid-point the company's own record supports for a normal year while a heavy capex programme still runs; management said any buyback decision would consider working-capital needs (S2), which argues against assuming the full boom-year ratio. It carries only the 0.15 div_yield weight and no weight in the primary DCF.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant — single-class share count, no issue planned; a buyback is under review but not executed (S2)

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zero: the DCF is a finite life-of-reserve value at the deck's long-run price and the engine's reserves line truncates production at the 2,883 Mt reserve base (F5), about 58 years at the revised delivery, and the life-end test stops the cash flows earlier still (FY2057E), so no perpetuity growth is added — the COAL peer convention (GEMS, BYAN).

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at 6.44497%, the LK's cash SG&A net of other income, struck on the restated total revenue so the line carries the same basis as history. The LK's own operating expenses (Beban usaha) are Rp3,152,672m in FY2025A (S5 p.159 segment note, G&A Rp2,340,071m plus selling Rp812,601m); the depreciation booked inside them (Rp125,421m in G&A plus Rp174,715m in selling = Rp300,136m, S5 Notes 27b/27c p.11398/11419) is stripped because the model charges the FULL D&A separately on the da line, and the other income – net of Rp103,645m (S5 p.17) is deducted so the ratio reproduces the LK's operating profit. That leaves Rp2,748,891m of cash SG&A over revenue Rp42,651,724m (F24). Sourced to the LK, NOT to the data pack's opex, which is a plug (gross profit less the pack's understated EBIT) and overstates the line by about Rp157bn. Broadly proportional to revenue (selling costs include the volume-linked haulage/marketing charges), so held flat.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E net profit of 7,629.6bn less the 9M print of 4,410.0bn implies Q4 net profit of 3,219.6bn, 1.82x Q3 1,766.6bn, at a 20.9% net margin against 12.5% for 9M. It is built on Q4 volume of 11.77 Mt and a Q4 ASP about 16-20% above the 9M average (FY 0.471 x 137.0 = 64.53 vs 9M 0.471 x 131.9 = 62.13), with unit cash cost held flat at IDR690,834/t (model fin.FY2026E.unit_cost), so about 83% of the Q4 price uplift falls to EBIT. No disclosed quarter shows a 21% net margin. At the 9M ASP the same volume gives FY2026E net profit of about 5.9trn (-22%) and DPS about 310, cutting the dividend-capacity anchor (3,370.2, -34.3% on price) by about 22%. Section 3 discloses the step-up qualitatively but gives no Q4 net profit, margin or the 9M-ASP sensitivity.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states the implied fourth quarter explicitly: net profit 3,156.9bn, a 17.6% net margin and a coal ASP 12.0% above the nine-month average, with the Q4 forward 149.35-153.30 labelled as the reviewed deck entry (S0, reviewed 2026-10-26) rather than a contracted price. Holding Q4 at the nine-month price is quantified: FY2026E net profit 6,295.9bn, DPS 328.1 and the dividend-capacity anchor 2,781, about a sixth below the base. This is disclosed, not assumed.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E volume of 44.0 Mt is 9M sales 32.23 Mt (F36) plus last year Q4 11.73 Mt, but 9M production was 34.41 Mt (F37), a 2.18 Mt inventory build, and Q3 production alone ran 14.96 Mt after H1 19.45 Mt. The company 2026 plan is 49.55 Mt production and 49.51 Mt sales (F42), which needs Q4 production 15.14 Mt and Q4 sales 17.28 Mt, i.e. a 2.14 Mt inventory draw that the build makes feasible. The report justifies 44.0 by the prior-year Q4 pace and does not reconcile the inventory or the Q3 production run-rate; if the inventory is drawn as the plan implies, FY2026E volume is 46-49 Mt. If transport is the binding constraint (coal transport 27.08 Mt, -9.8%, F47), that is not stated or sourced either.
challenges.answer: FY2026E volume raised from 44.0 to 47.0 Mt: 9M sales 32.23 Mt plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter production pace (Q3 production 14.96 Mt, +17% q/q after 19.45 Mt in H1). The 9M production-over-sales build of 2.18 Mt is carried as inventory rather than assumed sold. The transport constraint is stated: 27.08 Mt in 9M against a 41.0 Mt full-year target, so a 49.51 Mt sales year would need both a stock draw and a rail step-up; neither is assumed.

challenges.challenge: FY2027E volume of 49.5 Mt is sourced to F42, which says for 2026 PTBA set a production target of 49.55 Mt and sales of 49.51 Mt; it is the 2026 target, not a 2027 plan. S19 (27 Oct 2026) and S20 (30 Oct 2026) say the 2027 plan is still being submitted to ESDM and that the national target is ESDM call, with no tonnage published; approval is pending. The base nevertheless lifts volume 12.5% from FY2026E 44.0 in the year the Banko Barat permit expires (9 April 2027). The report says the company own plan and the last sourced forward level; for 2027 there is no sourced level.
challenges.answer: The report now says plainly that 49.5 Mt is the 2026 target held forward, not an approved 2027 plan: the 2027 RKAB is filed with ESDM and no 2027 tonnage is published (S19, S20). The approval risk is quantified at a 46 Mt delivered run-rate: the life DCF falls 5.1% and the target 3.7% (F91, F101). No approved 2027 tonnage is claimed anywhere.

challenges.challenge: capped_share 0.27 is set as half the 0.52-0.54 domestic share, but the report own data imply a larger capped volume. PLN group revenue was 30.7% of 9M revenue (10,803/35,200, F76) and 33.8% of FY2025 coal revenue (14,429.2/41,909.1, F58/F13); because PLN is the capped power buyer and pays below the average, its volume share must exceed its revenue share. At the average coal price the implied shares are 30.7% (9M) and 34.4% (FY2025), and 34-43% at a 10-20% discount. The assumption note says a 0.54 share truncates the DCF at FY2051 rather than FY2057, so the choice is value-relevant and the 0.27 is the optimistic end of the report own evidence.
challenges.answer: capped_share raised from 0.27 to 0.35 and derived from disclosed PLN revenue: 30.7% of 9M consolidated revenue (F67/F76) and 14,429.2bn, or 33.8%, of FY2025 coal revenue (F58/F13). Because PLN pays below the average, its volume share must exceed its revenue share; 0.35 is the low end of the implied 30.7-34.4% range. The DCF at 0.35 is the base, at 0.45 it is 1.1% lower, at 0.27 1.1% higher, and removing the cap adds 6.8%. The table is in section 4.

challenges.challenge: The model keeps nwc_pct at -0.48% and FY2026E delta_nwc at +910.8bn, but the 9M accounts show trade receivables up 1.89trn to 5.82trn (+47.9%, F69), PLN up 1.46trn to 2.68trn (+119%, F68) and total receivables 5,820bn against 3,930bn a year earlier. Receivables are now 16.5% of 9M revenue (5.82/35.20) against 12.5% (3.93/31.33) a year before. If that level is structural, FY2026E FCFF is overstated by about 1.0trn (about IDR85/share) and the 4.58trn FY2026 dividend (DPS 397.6) has thinner cash cover. The report flags the risk and says the full-year accounts are the test, but leaves the negative-NWC assumption unchanged and does not quantify the alternative.
challenges.answer: The receivables build is now stressed, not only flagged: holding net working capital at the nine-month run-rate cuts FY2026E FCFF to 2,558.2bn from 4,543.7bn and lowers the life DCF by 2.2% and the target by 0.8%. The modelled DPS and the dividend-capacity anchor do not move because they follow the payout rule, so the strain shows in cash cover, not in the anchor; the report says the full-year accounts decide whether the PLN balance unwinds. Ageing remains aggregate because PLN-level ageing is not disclosed.

challenges.challenge: Banko Barat (IUP 2402 K/30/MEM/2011) expires 9 April 2027 (S7 p.103) and produced 7,621,686 t in FY2025 (S7 p.26), 16.5% of Tanjung Enim total production of 46,261,672 t. The report calls renewal the largest single assumption in the valuation and says FY2027E volume depends on it, but no scenario tests non-renewal: the bear -5 Mt is attributed to RKAB/DMO and the DSI handover, not to the permit. A refusal or a delay past April removes up to about 16% of FY2027E volume and puts the 49.5 Mt base at risk at the same time as the unapproved 2027 plan.
challenges.answer: The Banko Barat effect is quantified and the permit is added to the catalyst list and the monitoring list: FY2025 production 7.62 Mt, 16.5% of Tanjung Enim (F87/F89); permanent non-renewal lowers the life DCF by 11.2% and the target by 8.5% (F90); 83.9% of the DCF present value sits after FY2027E (F99). No renewal application is disclosed in the annual report, the nine-month release or the 2027-plan reporting (S7, S19, S20); the report says so rather than asserting renewal.

challenges.challenge: The bull +0.5 Mt is justified by a 50 Mt RKAB-approved capacity, but S3 says the 2026 RKAB was approved without a volume cut at the 49.5 Mt target and S4 describes 50 Mt as a production ambition; no cited source states a 50 Mt approved ceiling. If the approved cap is 49.5 Mt, the bull 50.0 Mt is above it and the volume asymmetry justification is unsupported.
challenges.answer: The unsourced 50 Mt approved-capacity claim is removed. The bull volume shock is now zero: the base already runs at the approved 49.5 Mt 2026 target from FY2027E, S3 confirms the 2026 RKAB was approved at that target without a cut, and S4 50 Mt is a management aspiration. The volume asymmetry is justified as the bear continuing the delivered shortfall while the bull cannot exceed the approved target.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E realisation 0.471 is total 9M revenue of 35,200bn over 32.23 Mt, which includes the non-coal book; the report itself says this overstates the coal ASP by about 1.5% and that the coal-only ratio sits a shade below 0.471, previously carried at 0.4635. Using 0.471 overstates FY2026E coal revenue by about 0.7-0.8trn (about IDR40/share and about 1% of the DCF) for a disclosed reason, while the base is otherwise built on the coal-only physicals.
challenges.answer: FY2026E realisation corrected from 0.471 to 0.4635, the coal-only ratio: disclosed 9M revenue less the small non-coal book over 32.23 Mt, against the deck nine-month benchmark translated at the deck rupiah. This removes the double count of about 1.5% of coal revenue. The drift justification records the measured 9M ratio and the last-actual calibration it unwinds to.

challenges.challenge: The DCF stops at FY2057E with pv_sum 45,462bn, valuing about 1,530 Mt of the 2,883 Mt reserve base; the report says the full reserve-tail unlock adds a low-single-digit percentage to the bull value but gives no number, and the 5,713 Mt resource inventory and Ombilin are in no scenario. The method card treats resources as a free option rather than base NAV, but the report has already estimated the effect and withholds the figure, so the understatement cannot be seen or bounded.
challenges.answer: The tail is quantified: removing the DMO cap entirely adds 6.8% to the life DCF and 4.9% to the target, and that sensitivity is in section 4. It is excluded from the base and the bull because it requires an administrative price rise the state has not made. The resource inventory of 5,713 Mt against 2,883 Mt of reserves is stated in section 5, and Ombilin 102 Mt resources / 0 reserves is stated in sections 1 and 5, so the exclusion is visible and bounded.

challenges.challenge: Ombilin is called an option on the resource base, but the reserve table shows Ombilin resources of 102 Mt and reserves of 0 (S7 p.104, Ombilin 102 0 102 0); it is a resource option, not a reserve. Reactivation also needs an AMDAL and operating boundaries (S22) and its capex is not in the model. Calling it a free option without the 0-reserve/102 Mt resource fact and the unquantified reactivation capex overstates the optionality.
challenges.answer: Section 1 and section 5 now state that the annual report table carries Ombilin 102 Mt of resources and 0 Mt of reserves, so it sits outside the 2,883 Mt reserve base the DCF prices. The report also says the reactivation needs its AMDAL and operating boundaries around the UNESCO-listed Sawahlunto area, and that no reactivation capex, tonnage or schedule is published, so it cannot be modelled and is held as a resource option, not as value.

missing_bull_case.note: Two sourced upsides are understated. First, FY2026E volume of 44.0 Mt is below the 9M production run-rate: production was 34.41 Mt against 32.23 Mt sold (F37/F36), a 2.18 Mt build, and Q3 alone produced 14.96 Mt after H1 19.45 Mt; the company 2026 plan is 49.55 Mt production and 49.51 Mt sales (F42), which needs a 2.14 Mt Q4 inventory draw that the build makes feasible. Second, the DCF stops at FY2057E with pv_sum 45,462bn, valuing about 1,530 Mt of the 2,883 Mt reserve base, and the report says the full tail unlock adds a low-single-digit percentage to the bull without giving the number; the 5,713 Mt resource inventory is in no scenario. Both should be quantified, not asserted.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear does not test the two things that could break the base. First, the 9M receivables build: trade receivables rose 1.89trn to 5.82trn (+47.9%, F69) and PLN rose 1.46trn to 2.68trn (+119%, F68); the model keeps nwc_pct at -0.48% and FY2026E delta_nwc at +910.8bn, so a structural build is not stressed and the dividend cash cover is left untested. Second, Banko Barat (IUP 2402 K/30/MEM/2011, expiry 9 April 2027, S7 p.103) produced 7.62 Mt in FY2025, 16.5% of Tanjung Enim; the bear -5 Mt is attributed to RKAB/DMO and the DSI handover, never to a permit refusal or delay.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are mostly tied to the print, but the near-term volume path is not. FY2026E NP of 7,629.6bn minus the 9M 4,410.0bn implies Q4 NP 3,219.6bn, 1.82x Q3 1,766.6bn, at a 20.9% net margin against 12.5% for 9M, on Q4 volume 11.77 Mt and a Q4 ASP 16-20% above the 9M average while unit cash cost is held flat at IDR690,834/t. Meanwhile FY2027E volume 49.5 Mt is the 2026 target (F42), not a published 2027 plan, and capped_share 0.27 is below the 30.7-38% PLN volume share implied by its disclosed revenue. These are the three levers the C-challenges test.

evidence_and_citations.note: The load-bearing 9M, LK, permit, DSI and buyback facts verify. Three citation/definition problems remain. The bull +0.5 Mt is justified by a 50 Mt RKAB-approved capacity that no cited source states: S3 says the 2026 RKAB was approved at the 49.5 Mt target and S4 calls 50 Mt a production ambition. The realisation 0.471 is total revenue over tonnes, which the report itself says overstates the coal ratio by about 1.5% (coal-only is near 0.4635). And the price is the 29 October close (S0), six days before the 4 November asof; the price date is not stated in the note.

valuation_method_fit.note: Life-of-reserve DCF is the right primary and the bridge is complete and ties: net cash 4,317.1bn, minorities 112.6bn, associates 10,713.4bn and dividend payable 1,304.8bn give equity 59,075.2bn. The gaps are in the drivers, not the method: capped_share 0.27 is a heuristic (half the 0.52-0.54 domestic upper bound) that sets the year the DCF truncates and is below the company own PLN revenue share; the 25% EV/EBITDA anchor still applies 5.50x to FY2025A trough EBITDA of 5,222.2 (47% below FY2026E 11,156.1) with the -28% cross-check divergence explained only as trough; and the report gives no cost-curve quartile for the cost moat, which the method-card output contract requires. The 11.22% WACC is the top of the COAL set (AADI 10.19%, ITMG 10.30%).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is candid about the target sitting above the base (bull about 46% of the target), the implied Q4 step-up and the DCF-versus-anchor gap, and the rating survives a halved bull weight (base 65%, bear 25%, bull 10% still gives about Rp4,402 + DPS 398, a +57% total return). The one overreach is the cash-gap framing: "the earnings are real and the cash merely later" is inferred from aggregate ageing (1-30d 1.66trn, 31-90d 794.0bn, >90d 269.5bn) that does not break out PLN, which is about 46% of the book. The full-year accounts are the test and the report says so, but the summary states more than the evidence shows.
